issues.body: release.yml creates the Release via softprops/action-gh-release using the workflow's ordinary GITHUB_TOKEN. GitHub Actions intentionally prevents events generated by GITHUB_TOKEN from starting another workflow run (except workflow_dispatch/repository_dispatch). Therefore its release:published event will not launch release-verify.yml, so a normal v* release does not automatically produce the claimed verification log. The added self-test only checks that the trigger text exists and cannot expose this integration failure. This invalidates the repeated compliance/runbook claim that publishing the first release automatically yields a citable verdict.
issues.fix_hint: Run the verifier from the existing release.yml after the Create release step (or in a downstream job in that same workflow which needs the release job), where the published assets are already observable. Keep workflow_dispatch here if standalone re-verification is useful. Alternatively, explicitly create the Release with a suitably scoped GitHub App/PAT token whose event may trigger workflows, but that expands the credential/trust surface and should be tested and documented. Add a structural test that pins the verifier to the actual release-producing workflow rather than merely asserting a release:published trigger.
issues.title: The normal release path will not trigger this workflow

verdict.summary: The verification script and its hermetic tests are thoughtfully fail-closed, but the automatic execution path is not wired to the way this repository publishes releases. The existing release workflow creates the GitHub Release with its normal GITHUB_TOKEN; GitHub suppresses new workflow runs caused by events emitted with GITHUB_TOKEN. Consequently, the new release:published workflow will not run after the normal release.yml path, contradicting the central claim that the first tag automatically produces evidence.
